title: Synthetic diversity and change in nuclearity in [Co–Dy] coordination aggregates: bridge removal, solvent induced structural reorganization and AC susceptibility measurements

material_class.structural_family: vertex-shared {Dy3Co4} dicubane cation with mononuclear Dy-pivalate counteranion

synthesis.procedure: To a solution of H2L1 (0.0165 g, 0.1 mmol) in MeOH (2 mL) was added Dy(NO3)3·5H2O (0.044 g, 0.1 mmol) in MeOH (2 mL). After stirring 10 min, Co2(μ-OH2)(O2CCMe3)4(HO2CCMe3)4 (0.0474 g, 0.05 mmol) in MeOH was added, giving a light red-brown solution. After 15 min, Et3N (55.6 μL, 0.4 mmol) was added, the mixture was stirred 3 h, and filtered on a G4 sintered bed. Slow evaporation of the filtrate at room temperature over one month gave red block crystals of 1.
synthesis.vessel_or_method: solution synthesis; G4 sintered-bed filtration; slow evaporation
synthesis.workup_and_crystallization: filtered; slow evaporation of filtrate at room temperature over one month afforded red block-shaped crystals

properties.summary: DC magnetometry of 1 shows χmT = 60.45 cm3 K mol−1 at 290 K (0.1 T), consistent with four DyIII plus two high-spin CoII (and diamagnetic CoIII). Magnetization at 2 K reaches 25.4 NAμB at 5 T without saturation. A non-zero out-of-phase AC susceptibility signal is observed under zero static bias field, without maxima in χM″(T) in the measured window. UV–vis absorption bands of MeCN solutions are reported.

measurements.name: AC out-of-phase susceptibility χM″
measurements.conditions: zero static bias field; frequencies indicated in Fig. 8; AC 3–1000 Hz, 1.8–50 K

source_locations.location: Magnetic DC/AC discussion; Fig. 7a and Fig. 8; UV-vis in synthesis of 1

material_class.structural_family: vertex-shared {Dy3Co4} dicubane cation with mononuclear Dy-pivalate counteranion

synthesis.procedure: To H2L2 (0.0195 g, 0.1 mmol) in MeOH (2 mL) was added dropwise Co2(μ-OH2)(O2CCMe3)4(HO2CCMe3)4 (0.0474 g, 0.05 mmol) in MeOH (2 mL), giving a light red-brown solution. After 10 min stirring, Et3N (55.6 μL, 0.4 mmol) was added and the mixture stirred 30 min, then treated with Dy(NO3)3·5H2O (0.044 g, 0.1 mmol) in MeOH (1 mL). The solution was stirred 3 h, filtered, and the filtrate slowly evaporated over one month to give red block crystals of 2.
synthesis.workup_and_crystallization: filtered; slow evaporation of filtrate over one month afforded red block-shaped crystals

properties.summary: χmT = 59.88 cm3 K mol−1 at 290 K (0.1 T). Magnetization at 2 K reaches 26.9 NAμB at 5 T without saturation. Unlike 1, AC susceptibility of 2 shows no significant out-of-phase component down to 1.8 K and up to 1000 Hz, with or without static bias fields up to 0.2 T. UV–vis absorption of MeCN solutions is reported.

measurements.value: no significant χ″ down to 1.8 K
measurements.conditions: 3–1000 Hz; zero field and static bias up to 0.2 T

source_locations.location: Magnetic DC/AC discussion; Fig. 7a; Fig. S18; UV-vis in synthesis of 2

material_class.structural_family: hexanuclear near-planar {Dy2Co4} aggregate from MeCN-induced reorganization of 2

synthesis.procedure: Red block crystals of 2 (0.029 g, 0.01 mmol) were treated with 2 mL MeCN for partial dissolution. The suspension stood overnight in a capped vial, giving a clear red solution. Light red block crystals appeared after two weeks and were grown for a month, then collected for single-crystal X-ray analysis. Formation is driven by loss of OMe− bridges and DyIII from the heptanuclear core of 2 in MeCN.
synthesis.time: overnight dissolution; crystals after 2 weeks; collected after 1 month
synthesis.workup_and_crystallization: standing of MeCN solution under capped conditions; light red block crystals grown over a month
synthesis.yield: 40% (experimental section; 51% also stated in results discussion)
